Coarsen to Cohorts with Equal Widths

Source: R/cohort_coarsen.R
cohort_coarsen_five.Rd

Coarsen the cohorts defined by labels. The new cohorts must contain the old cohorts, and (except for open cohorts) all have the same width.

  • cohort_coarsen_five() Five-year cohorts

  • cohort_coarsen_ten() Ten-year cohorts

Usage

cohort_coarsen_five(
  labels,
  offset = 0,
  open_left = NULL,
  open_right = NULL,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

cohort_coarsen_ten(
  labels,
  offset = 0,
  open_left = NULL,
  open_right = NULL,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

Arguments

labels

Vector of cohort labels.

offset

Parameter controlling alignment of cohorts. Default is 0.

open_left

Whether to include a cohort that is open on the left. Optional. See below for details.

open_right

Whether to include a cohort that is open on the right. Optional. See below for details.

interpret_single

How to interpret a label for a single year, such as "2020". Choices are "lower" (the default) and "upper". See below for details.

interpret_multi

How to interpret a label that refers to multiple years, such as "2020-2025". Choices are NULL (the default), "at_upper", and "below_upper". See below for details.

interpret_fail

Action if element of labels cannot be interpreted. Choices are "error" (the default), "warn", and "silent".

Value

Factor with the same length as labels.

Details

The new cohorts cannot split existing cohorts, and are typically wider than the existing cohorts.

If labels is a factor, its levels are modified along with its elements.

Rules for interpreting inputs

Single-year

Labels for single-year cohorts sometimes refer to the lower limits of cohorts, and sometimes refer to upper limits. For instance, the label "2020" is sometimes used to refer to the cohort that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2021, and is sometimes used to refer to the cohort that starts at midnight on 1 July 2019 and ends at midnight on 1 July 2020.

The interpret_single argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_singleRuleExample
"lower""a" -> [a,a+1)"2020" -> [2020,2021)
"upper""a" -> [a-1,a)"2020" -> [2019,2020)

Multi-year

In labels for multi-year cohorts, the second number is sometimes the upper limit of the cohort, and sometimes the upper limit minus 1. For instance, the cohort that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2025 is sometimes labelled "2020-2025" and is sometimes labelled "2020-2024".

The interpret_multi argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_multiRuleExample
"at_upper""a-b" -> [a,b)"2020-2025" -> [2020,2025)
"below_upper""a-b" -> [a,b+1)"2020-2024" -> [2020,2025)

If interpret_multi is NULL (the default), then multi-year labels are interpreted using the "at_upper" convention. If, however, the "at_upper" convention leads to intervals with widths 4, 9, 14, ..., then agetime emits a message. Supplying an explicit value for interpret_multi silences this message.

Open

A cohort that is open on the left has no lower limit, and a cohort that is open on the right has no upper limit. Labels for open cohorts are not affected by interpret_single or interpret_multi.

Some examples of open cohorts:

LabelInterval
"<2000", "before 2000", "under 2000"(-Inf,2000)
"2000 or earlier", "up to 2000"(-Inf,2001)
"2000+", "2000 or more", "2000 or later"[2000,Inf)

Labels starting with "-", such as "-2000", are not accepted.

The open_left argument

A cohort is open on the left if it has no lower limit, e.g. "<2000".

By default, the return value has a cohort that is open on the left if and only if labels does. The full range of options is:

open_leftlabels has open on leftReturn value has open on left
NULL (default)YesYes
NULL (default)NoNo
TRUEYesYes
TRUENoYes
FALSEYesError
FALSENoNo

The open_right argument

A cohort is open on the right if it has no upper limit, e.g. "2000+".

By default, the return value has a cohort that is open on the right if and only if labels does. The full range of options is:

open_rightlabels has open on rightReturn value has open on right
NULL (default)YesYes
NULL (default)NoNo
TRUEYesYes
TRUENoYes
FALSEYesError
FALSENoNo

  • age_coarsen_five() Age equivalent of cohort_coarsen_five()

  • age_coarsen_ten() Age equivalent of cohort_coarsen_ten()

  • period_coarsen_ten() Period equivalent of cohort_coarsen_ten()

Examples

labels <- c("2002-2004", "1987-1989", "2000", "Total")
cohort_coarsen_five(labels)
#> [1] 2000-2005 1985-1990 2000-2005 Total    
#> Levels: 1985-1990 2000-2005 Total
cohort_coarsen_ten(labels)
#> [1] 2000-2010 1980-1990 2000-2010 Total    
#> Levels: 1980-1990 2000-2010 Total

## align to different boundaries
cohort_coarsen_five(labels, offset = 2)
#> [1] 2002-2007 1987-1992 1997-2002 Total    
#> Levels: 1987-1992 1997-2002 2002-2007 Total

## let inclusion of open cohort depend on labels
cohort_coarsen_five(c("2010", "2020-2025"))
#> [1] 2010-2015 2020-2025
#> Levels: 2010-2015 2020-2025

## insist on an open cohort
cohort_coarsen_five(c("2010", "2020-2025"), open_left = TRUE)
#> [1] <2015     2020-2025
#> Levels: <2015 2020-2025
